references.text: Isaiah describes how the Lord raises a banner for a people from afar who come swiftly—a parallel to the threat of a distant nation in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah prophesies about a people from afar coming against Israel, a people with an unknown language—a direct parallel to the words concerning a foreign tongue.
The eagle swooping down is used as an image of an enemy attacking, employing the same imagery found in Deuteronomy.
The eagle flying and spreading its wings is used as a picture of an attacker, paralleling the eagle metaphor in Deuteronomy.
Ezekiel uses the image of a great eagle to represent a foreign nation coming, employing the same symbolism as in Deuteronomy.
Hosea uses the image of the eagle coming over the Lord's house because of disobedience, a direct allusion to the curse in Deuteronomy.
Habakkuk describes the Chaldeans flying like eagles to devour, using the same imagery as the prophecy in Deuteronomy.
Jesus uses the eagle metaphor in connection with judgment and gathering, which can be related to the speed and inevitability of the eagle.
